note: Grade 3. The year decoding stops being the bottleneck and comprehension becomes the work. Morphology carries most of the vocabulary growth from here on.

skills.name: Reads longer words by chunking them
skills.description: Three syllables and up: fan-tas-tic, im-por-tant. Splitting is the skill, not sounding out.

skills.name: Reads common prefixes
Reads common suffixes
Finds the root inside a longer word
skills.description: Seeing 'help' in 'unhelpfully' turns one known word into a family.

probe.prompt: What is the root word in {word}?

skills.name: Reads irregular plurals
Tells homophones apart in context
skills.description: there/their/they're. Only the sentence can decide.

skills.name: Reads grade-3 text at a comfortable rate
skills.description: Roughly 110-120 correct words per minute by year end. Rate is a symptom of decoding, never the goal.

skills.name: Reads silently and remembers it
skills.description: The shift from reading aloud to reading to yourself. Comprehension often dips here before it recovers.

skills.name: Names the main idea and the details that support it

probe.prompt: What is this mostly about? Which two sentences tell you that?

skills.name: Summarises without retelling everything
skills.description: Deciding what to leave out is the skill. Most children retell instead.

probe.prompt: Tell me what happened in three sentences.

skills.name: Explains why something happened
Explains why a character did something
skills.description: Requires holding what a character wants against what they do.

probe.prompt: Why did she do that? What did she want?

skills.name: Points to the part of the text that proves it
skills.description: The habit that separates an answer from a guess.

probe.prompt: Show me where it says that.

skills.name: Notices how a text is organised
skills.description: In order, compared, problem and solution.

skills.name: Tells who is telling the story

probe.prompt: Who is telling this? How would it be different if the other character told it?

skills.name: Pulls information from two texts on one topic

probe.prompt: What did you learn from both? What did only one of them say?

skills.name: Works out a word from its prefix, root, and suffix
skills.description: The single highest-leverage vocabulary skill there is. One root unlocks a dozen words.

probe.prompt: What do you think {word} means? What parts do you recognise?

skills.name: Tells apart words that nearly mean the same
skills.description: Warm, hot, scorching. Precision rather than synonyms.

skills.name: Understands sayings that do not mean what they say
skills.description: Raining cats and dogs. Often the sticking point for literal-minded readers.

probe.prompt: What does it really mean when we say {phrase}?

skills.name: Looks a word up

probe.prompt: Find what this word means. Which meaning fits our sentence?
